body:
We should be able to do /enqueue and /after commands, which will only execute one task, after the task we reply to finished.

It should use some of /stop, /log, /watch mechanics, yet work as /solve, /claude, /codex commands.

So we reply by UUID or issue/pull request urls, and put that task in queue with a condition that our new task may be only started after selected task finishes successfully, on fail the pending task also should fail, as we treat /after as only only on success requirement.

That will allow to manually construct a correct queue of tasks, so all blockers are done first and we can model queue after  actual planned development process. So we respect all dependencies between tasks.

We also should add `--respect-blockers` for /solve, /claude, /codex commands, that will mean, that if the not all blockers are resolved in GitHub blockers relationships between tasks, we don't allow to start that task on its own, but if we have blockers in the queue already, we queue our new task like `/after` the blockers (specified on GitHub).

Also in previous https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/pull/4068 we should `--respect-blockers` by default, and execute all batch issues in such and order, that we execute unblocked already tasks first.

So we do it carefully and nicely. And user will have ability to perfectly support the development process with no violation of any dependencies.

Also in /hive command by default, we also should respect order of blockers/dependencies/child/parent relationships on GitHub when executed in any specified concurrency.

We should also treat not only direct blockers, but also sub-issues as blockers for parent issue.

We should double check in all other related places in codebase we do it exactly perfectly. If there options on how to handle it we should have configuration, with specified vision by default.

Also if we have other open issues related to this topic, we should also highlight them in our pull request, and if they are exactly the same as described vision we can fix/close them as part of this single pull request.

If open issues related to that topic have different vision we just list them as possible related to.

If we have any bugs in codebase on the topic (directly related to this vision) with or without open issues, we should all fix them in this pull request.

`--respect-blockers` for /solve, /claude, /codex commands is experimental by default (meaning it is turned off), but in all other places were it may be important to handle relationships between issues, we should enable it by default.
 
We need to collect data related about the issue to this repository, make sure we compile that data to `./docs/case-studies/issue-{id}` folder, and use it to do deep case study analysis (also make sure to search online for additional facts and data), list of each and all requirements from the issue, and propose possible solutions and solution plans for each requirement (we should also check known existing components/libraries, that solve similar problem or can help in solutions).

Please plan and execute everything in this single pull request, you have unlimited time and context, as context auto-compacts and you can continue indefinitely, until each and every requirement fully addressed, and everything is totally done.
title: /enqueue, /after commands
